content.user_title: Design MCP Prompts for AI Workflows
content.value_statement: MCP server authors need prompt templates that are clear, reusable, and easy to test. This skill provides practical rmcp patterns for arguments, context, examples, and conversation flows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how MCP prompts expose reusable message templates to users.
Shows Rust rmcp examples for listing prompts and returning prompt responses.
Demonstrates required and optional prompt arguments with default values.
Covers prompt patterns for code review, API design, learning, debugging, and refactoring.
Includes examples for context-rich prompts, few-shot prompts, and prompt tests.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a complete ready-to-run MCP server.
Focuses on Rust rmcp patterns and may need adaptation for other SDKs.
Does not include automated validation for prompt injection resistance.
Example snippets use simplified error handling for teaching purposes.

use_cases.title: Build Prompt Templates
use_cases.description: Create reusable prompts with clear names, descriptions, required arguments, and structured messages.

use_cases.title: Add Project Context
use_cases.description: Design prompts that include documentation, examples, dependencies, and project guidelines before the user task.

use_cases.title: Test Prompt Behavior
use_cases.description: Plan unit and integration tests that verify prompt listing, argument handling, and response structure.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first MCP prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a basic MCP prompt named [prompt_name]. It should take [required_argument] and guide the assistant to [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Design Prompt Arguments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my prompt goal: [goal]. Suggest required arguments, optional arguments, defaults, and validation rules for an MCP prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Add Context Injection
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt with project or reference context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MCP prompt for [task] that injects [context_sources]. Include message structure, context sections, and safeguards for irrelevant context.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Prompt Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this MCP prompt design for clarity, argument safety, context quality, test coverage, and user experience. Return concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: Request: Create a prompt for reviewing Rust code with a security focus.
output_examples.output: A structured prompt plan with language and focus arguments, review goals, security checks, and expected response sections.

output_examples.input: Request: Add project context to an MCP prompt for a refactoring task.
output_examples.output: A context layout that includes project name, language, framework, dependencies, task details, and implementation guidelines.

output_examples.input: Request: Test an MCP prompt that requires one argument.
output_examples.output: A test plan that checks prompt discovery, missing argument errors, valid responses, and message content expectations.

best_practices: Define clear prompt names, descriptions, and argument requirements before writing message content.
Validate dynamic arguments before inserting them into prompt text or system messages.
Test each prompt with valid inputs, missing inputs, and realistic user tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not hide important behavior inside vague prompt descriptions.
Do not insert untrusted arguments into high-authority messages without review.
Do not ship prompts without tests for required arguments and response structure.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design MCP prompt templates for AI assistants using Rust rmcp examples.

faq.question: Does it create a complete MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It provides prompt design guidance and examples that you can adapt into your server.

faq.question: Which SDK does the guide use?
faq.answer: The examples use the Rust rmcp crate and common MCP prompt response structures.

faq.question: Can I use the ideas with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompt patterns are useful for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other MCP clients.

faq.question: Does the guide cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes unit and integration testing patterns for prompt listing and prompt responses.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing prompts?
faq.answer: Review argument validation, context quality, message authority, and tests for missing or unusual inputs.
